mainTopic: Identifying the author of a ברייתא about רבי יהושע's view, five separate מעילות, and רבי עקיבא's question to רבי אליעזר about many מלאכות on many שבתות
overview: The amud opens by asking who wrote a ברייתא about eating from one offering cooked in five pots. Is it רבי עקיבא or רבי יהושע? Its two halves point in opposite directions, so the גמרא says תנאים disagree about whether רבי יהושע accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation. The גמרא also suggests the author could follow רבי עקיבא on הַעֲלָמָה while disagreeing with him about מעילות. Next, several אמוראים explain how one offering can produce five separate מעילות: five parts of the עולה, five limbs, one shoulder, five kinds of cooked dishes, or five flavors. A new משנה follows, in which רבי עקיבא asks רבי אליעזר about doing many תולדות of one מלאכה on many שבתות in one lapse of awareness. רבי אליעזר answers with a קל וחומר from נדה, and the two go back and forth over minor girls and an animal. The גמרא then asks what exactly רבי עקיבא was asking, and רבא answers that he asked two questions at once. Finally, the גמרא asks which kind of mistake the many-שבתות question was about. רבה begins to answer, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא never mentions a doubt offering, so who wrote it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא does not mention an אשם תלוי for a case of doubt, and asks who its author is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yet the ברייתא does not say that if he is unsure whether he ate it, he brings an אשם תלוי. So whose opinion is this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out something missing from the ברייתא and asks who wrote it. This is a setup: figuring out the author will tell us what רבי יהושע held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists when a person brings חטאות but says nothing about a case of doubt. Leaving that out is a clue about which תנא is speaking. If we can pin down the author, we can learn whether רבי יהושע accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: His doubt about it, when he is not sure whether he ate it
A 'provisional' guilt offering brought when one is unsure whether he sinned
It does not teach, meaning the text leaves this out
Whose opinion is this?

phrases.english: And yet, regarding a case of doubt about it,
phrases.notes: He means a case where he isn't sure whether he ate from it at all.

phrases.english: that he brings a provisional guilt offering, it does not teach.
Whose opinion is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי הָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא being examined to learn whether רבי יהושע accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the author of the ברייתא that leaves out the אשם תלוי for a doubt?

steps.title: It cannot be רבי עקיבא, who requires an אשם תלוי even for doubtful מעילה
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא were the author, the ברייתא should have taught an אשם תלוי for a doubt, since he requires one even for doubtful מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי עקיבא, then the end of the ברייתא should also say, 'And if he is unsure about them, he brings an אשם תלוי.' After all, a משנה teaches that רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי even for doubtful מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the idea that רבי עקיבא wrote the ברייתא and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא applies אשם תלוי broadly, even to doubtful מעילה. If he were the author, the ברייתא would surely have mentioned the doubt case. Since it doesn't, the author is probably not רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, used to suggest a possibility the גמרא will test
The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
A doubt whether one misused הקדש (consecrated property)
Holds a person liable (to bring an offering)

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Akiva,
let it also teach in the last clause:
'And for a doubt about them, he brings a provisional guilt offering,'
for we learned in a Mishnah: Rabbi Akiva holds one liable
phrases.notes: This is the משנה later in this מסכת, on 22b.

phrases.english: to bring a provisional guilt offering for a doubtful misuse of consecrated property!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, לִיתְנֵי נָמֵי סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible author and rules him out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי even for doubtful מעילה, so a ברייתא by him would have mentioned the doubt case. It doesn't.

steps.title: So it is רבי יהושע, and it seems he accepted רבי עקיבא's point
steps.stepSummary: If the author is רבי יהושע, the ruling 'five lapses, five חטאות' suggests he accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: So isn't it רבי יהושע? And the ברייתא teaches: 'With five lapses of awareness, he brings five חטאות.' Learn from this that רבי יהושע accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: Once רבי עקיבא is ruled out, the גמרא says the author must be רבי יהושע. It then reads the first part of the ברייתא as proof that he changed his mind and agreed with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא requires five חטאות only when there were five separate lapses of awareness. That implies one lapse means only one חטאת for the one offering in five pots, which is רבי עקיבא's position. If רבי יהושע taught this, he must have accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it…? Used to propose the remaining option
Lapses of awareness, separate times of forgetting
Sin offerings
Learn from this, introducing a conclusion
He accepted it from him (agreed to the refutation)

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it Rabbi Yehoshua?
And it teaches: 'With five lapses of awareness,'
'he brings five sin offerings,'
So learn from this that he accepted it from him!
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע, and 'it' is רבי עקיבא's refutation in the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: With רבי עקיבא ruled out, names רבי יהושע as author and draws a proof from the ברייתא's first part.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's ruling that five lapses bring five חטאות, implying one lapse brings only one

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא suggests the opposite
steps.stepSummary: The last part of the ברייתא makes one liable for each of five offerings even in one lapse, which suggests רבי יהושע did not accept the refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, look at the end of the ברייתא: 'From five offerings, even in one lapse of awareness, he is liable for each one.' Learn from this that רבי יהושע did not accept רבי עקיבא's refutation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back with the other half of the same ברייתא, which seems to prove the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last part says eating from five different offerings in one lapse makes him liable for each one. The גמרא reads this as רבי יהושע's original view still standing, so he did not accept the refutation. Now the two halves of the ברייתא seem to point in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary, the opposite is true
Offerings (animal sacrifices)
A single lapse of awareness
Each and every one

phrases.english: But on the contrary, from the last clause, which teaches:
'From five offerings, even in one lapse of awareness,'
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'one.'

phrases.english: 'he is liable for each and every one,'
So learn from this that he did not accept it from him!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַדְּרַבָּה, מִסֵּיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3's proof with a contrary inference from the same ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the conclusion that רבי יהושע accepted the refutation
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof looked only at the first part. The last part of the ברייתא points the other way.
steps.confusionAlert: Both inferences come from the SAME ברייתא: the first part points one way and the last part points the other. Don't think the גמרא brought a new source here.

steps.title: A dispute between תנאים about what רבי יהושע held
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא points both ways, the גמרא suggests that different תנאים disagree about whether רבי יהושע accepted the refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: So what can you say? It must be a dispute between תנאים. One תנא holds that רבי יהושע accepted the refutation, and another תנא holds that he did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the clash between the two parts of the ברייתא by saying they reflect two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each half of the ברייתא follows a different תנא's report of רבי יהושע's final view. One תנא holds he accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation, and the other holds he did not. The way the גמרא phrases it, 'what can you say?', shows it treats this as the only way left to explain the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what else can you say? Leads into the only way left to explain the text
It is a dispute between תנאים
A sage of the משנה era, or the teacher of a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two parts lead to opposite conclusions about רבי יהושע. So the גמרא says תנאים disagree about whether he accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation.

phrases.english: Rather, what is there for you to say?
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording; some versions don't have it.

phrases.english: It is a dispute between tanna'im,
for there is a tanna who holds that he accepted it,
and there is a tanna who holds that he did not accept it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא מַאי אִית לָךְ לְמֵימַר, תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction between step 3 and step 4 by splitting the ברייתא between two תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two parts of the ברייתא to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole ברייתא follows one view of רבי יהושע, so it should prove one clear answer.
steps.terutzMaskana: תנאים disagree about whether רבי יהושע accepted רבי עקיבא's refutation, and the two parts of the ברייתא reflect the two views.

steps.title: The ברייתא can follow רבי עקיבא after all
steps.stepSummary: Now that the ברייתא may be split between different תנאים, the גמרא says its author could be רבי עקיבא's follower. He agrees with רבי עקיבא about הַעֲלָמָה and disagrees with him about מעילות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא. This תנא agrees with him on one point and disagrees on another. He agrees with him about a lapse of awareness, but disagrees with him about misusing holy property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the difficulty raised in step 2: why the ברייתא does not mention an אשם תלוי if it follows רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that רבי עקיבא requires an אשם תלוי even for doubtful מעילה, yet the ברייתא leaves it out. The answer: the author follows רבי עקיבא only on the rule about one lapse of awareness. On מעילה he disagrees and does not require an אשם תלוי for a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A lapse of awareness: the time one keeps sinning without realizing it is forbidden
Cases of misusing holy (הקדש) property
He agrees with his opinion
He disagrees with him
A 'hanging' guilt offering brought when one is unsure whether he sinned

steps.whatToRemember: A תנא can follow a great sage on one rule and still argue with him on another. That is how this ברייתא can follow רבי עקיבא and still leave out the אשם תלוי.

phrases.english: You may even say it is Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי תַּנָּא סָבַר לַהּ כְּוָתֵיהּ בַּחֲדָא
phrases.english: and this tanna holds like him in one matter
and disagrees with him in one matter:
he holds like him regarding a lapse of awareness,
and disagrees with him regarding misuse of holy property.
phrases.notes: So this תנא does not require an אשם תלוי for a doubt about מעילה. That is why the ברייתא never mentions one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 5's idea of splitting the ברייתא and uses it to answer step 2's difficulty with רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the opinion: the author follows רבי עקיבא on one issue but not on another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, it should have taught an אשם תלוי for a doubtful case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The author agrees with רבי עקיבא about הַעֲלָמָה but disagrees with him about מעילות, so no אשם תלוי is mentioned.

steps.title: How can there be five separate misuses?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case is meant by 'five מעילות', where one is liable five separate times for misusing holy property.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of five misuses of holy property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question about the case of 'five מעילות' mentioned earlier. It is setting up a list of answers from several אמוראים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case speaks of eating pieces that all come from a single offering. The puzzle is what makes these five separate acts of מעילה instead of one. The answers that follow each suggest what makes the pieces count separately.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: What is the case of five misuses of holy property?

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי חָמֵשׁ מְעִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of who wrote the ברייתא and opens a new question about defining the case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of eating makes someone liable for five separate מעילות.

steps.title: שמואל: five different parts of the עולה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the case is like the משנה that lists five parts of a עולה which join together: meat, fat, wine, flour and oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is like what we learned: five things in a burnt offering join together: the meat, the fat, the wine, the fine flour and the oil.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the first answer. The five מעילות come from eating five different parts that belong to a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל points to a known משנה that lists five separate parts of a עולה. Each part is a different kind of thing, so using each one counts as its own מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח
They join together to make up a required amount
Forbidden fat of an animal
Fine flour, used for the מנחה brought with the קרבן

phrases.english: Shmuel said: Like that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מעילה 15b.

phrases.english: Five things in a burnt offering join together:
the meat, and the fat, and the wine,
and the fine flour, and the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כְּאוֹתָהּ שֶׁשָּׁנִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five different kinds of parts of the offering (meat, fat, wine, flour, oil).

steps.title: חזקיה: five different limbs
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the case is someone who ate from five different limbs of the offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: For example, where he ate from five limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives a second answer: the five מעילות come from five different limbs of the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike שמואל, חזקיה stays with the meat of the animal itself. Separate limbs are separate enough to count as five separate misuses.

keyTerms.meaning: Limbs or body parts of the animal
For example; such as

phrases.english: Chizkiyya said:
For example, where he ate from five limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: חִזְקִיָּה אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל מֵחֲמִשָּׁה אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question from step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Eating from five different limbs of the animal.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: even one limb, the shoulder
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says it can happen even within one limb, as in the shoulder.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: You can even say it is in one limb; you find it in the shoulder.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש goes further than חזקיה and says five separate limbs are not needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה needed five limbs. ריש לקיש says a single limb like the shoulder is enough, because it has distinct sections that can count separately.

keyTerms.meaning: One single limb
You can find it; this case happens
Shoulder

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּאֵבֶר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: You can even say in one limb,
you find it in the shoulder.
phrases.notes: He means the shoulder has several different sections, so five pieces from it can still count as five.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בְּאֵבֶר אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens חזקיה's answer: even one limb is enough.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Five pieces from one limb, such as the shoulder.

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: five kinds of cooked dishes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says the case is someone who ate the meat prepared as five different kinds of pot dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא said: For example, where he ate from five kinds of pot dishes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא gives another answer: the difference comes from how the meat was cooked, not which part of the animal it came from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the five pieces may come from the same spot on the animal. Because they were cooked as five different kinds of dishes, each one counts separately.

keyTerms.meaning: Kinds of pot dishes; different ways of cooking

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha said:
For example, where he ate in five kinds of pot dishes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל בַּחֲמִשָּׁה מִינֵי קְדֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to step 7, based on cooking instead of body parts.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat prepared as five different kinds of cooked dishes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: five different flavors
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the case is someone who ate meat with five different flavors.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: For example, where he ate it with five flavors.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the last answer: five pieces seasoned with five different flavors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן makes the line even finer than cooking style. Different seasonings alone are enough to make each piece count as its own מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Flavors, such as from different seasonings

steps.whatToRemember: There are five answers to 'what is five מעילות': five parts of the עולה (שמואל), five limbs (חזקיה), one limb like the shoulder (ריש לקיש), five kinds of cooked dishes (רבי יצחק נפחא), and five flavors (רבי יוחנן).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
For example, where he ate with five flavors.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁאָכַל בַּחֲמִשָּׁה טְעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final answer to the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pieces seasoned with five different flavors.

steps.title: New משנה: רבי עקיבא's question to רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. רבי עקיבא asked רבי אליעזר about someone who did many תולדות of one מלאכה on many שבתות, all in one lapse of awareness. Is he liable once, or for each one?
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי עקיבא said: I asked רבי אליעזר about someone who does many מלאכות on many שבתות, all of the same type of מלאכה, in one lapse of awareness. What is the law? Is he liable once for all of them, or for each and every one?
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a question רבי עקיבא put to his teacher רבי אליעזר. The answer comes in the next part of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things make this case hard: there are many שבתות, which might split the sins apart, and many acts that all belong to one type of מלאכה, which might join them. Everything happened in one lapse of awareness, which usually means one קרבן. The question is which factor wins.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, our משנה
The kinds of work forbidden on שבת
Of the same kind as one main מלאכה (its sub-types)
One single lapse of awareness
Each and every one

steps.confusionAlert: All the acts belong to one main type of מלאכה, so this is not a case of breaking several different אבות מלאכה. The case raises two issues at once: whether the many שבתות split the sins, and whether different sub-types of one מלאכה count separately. The גמרא spells this out in step 23.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said: I asked Rabbi Eliezer
about one who does many labors
on many Shabbatot
all of the same type as one main labor
in one lapse of awareness, what is the law?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording; both mean 'one'.

phrases.english: Is he liable once for all of them,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: or is he liable for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic, separate from the discussion of מעילות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה presents the question: with many שבתות, one type of מלאכה and one lapse of awareness, is there one obligation or many?

steps.title: רבי אליעזר answers: liable for each one, by a קל וחומר from נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר rules that the person brings a separate חטאת for each act, and proves it with a קל וחומר from נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is liable for each and every one. This comes from a קל וחומר. Take a נדה, where there are not many kinds of acts that lead to sin and many sin offerings, and still he is liable for each and every act. So by שבת, where there are many kinds of acts that lead to sin and many death penalties, surely he should be liable for each and every one!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר answers the question from the previous step: the person is liable for each act separately. He backs this up with a קל וחומר from the laws of נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נדה there is only one kind of forbidden act, and yet each act of relations brings its own חטאת. שבת is 'stricter' because it has many forbidden kinds of labor and many death penalties. So if the 'lighter' case of נדה splits into many חטאות, the 'heavier' case of שבת surely should too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a heavier one: if the light case has this law, the heavy case surely does
A woman in her menstrual state, with whom relations are forbidden
Literally 'outcomes': different kinds of acts that lead to a sin
Sin offerings, brought for an accidental sin
Death penalties (for doing it on purpose)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת,
phrases.english: He said to him: He is liable for each and every one,
from a kal vachomer:
Just as a niddah, which does not have
many forms of sin and many sin offerings –
one is liable for each and every one,
Shabbat, which has
many forms of sin and many death penalties –

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁיְּהֵא חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאֶחָת?
phrases.english: is it not logical that he should be liable for each and every one?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת, מִקַּל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's question from step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether many תולדות on many שבתות in one lapse bring one חטאת or many.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A separate חטאת for each one, proven by a קל וחומר from נדה.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: נדה has two prohibitions, שבת only one
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the קל וחומר: נדה is stricter in another way, because both the man and the woman are warned.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: You can say that about נדה, which has two warnings, since he is warned about the נדה and the נדה is warned about him. But can you say it about שבת, which has only one warning?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא, telling the story, says he pushed back on רבי אליעזר's קל וחומר. He points out a way that נדה is actually stricter than שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'light' case is light in every way. רבי עקיבא shows that נדה has something שבת lacks: two prohibitions, one on the man and one on the woman. That extra strictness could be why each act of relations counts separately, so you cannot carry the rule over to שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning, meaning a Torah prohibition
Warned, meaning under a prohibition
'If you said it about X, will you say it about Y?': the standard way to knock down a קל וחומר

phrases.english: I said to him: If you said this about a niddah,
phrases.notes: "I" is רבי עקיבא, telling over his conversation with רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: which has two prohibitions,
since he is prohibited regarding the niddah
and the niddah is prohibited regarding him,

phrases.aramaic: תֹּאמַר בַּשַּׁבָּת, שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ אֶלָּא אַזְהָרָה אֶחָת!
phrases.english: will you say it about Shabbat, which has only one prohibition?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּנִּדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison of שבת to נדה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: נדה has a strictness שבת lacks: two prohibitions (man and woman), so it is not the 'lighter' case.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: minor girls prove it, with only one prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר brings the case of relations with a minor נדה: only one prohibition, yet liable for each act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: One who has relations with minor girls will prove it. There is only one warning there, and still he is liable for each and every act!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his argument. He brings a case of נדה where there is only one prohibition, and the rule still holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A minor girl is not obligated in מצוות, so only the man is under a prohibition. Yet he still brings a separate חטאת for each act. This shows the 'two prohibitions' point is not the reason for the rule, so רבי עקיבא's objection falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Will prove': brings a case that shows an objection is wrong
Minor girls, not yet obligated in מצוות

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת יוֹכִיחַ,
phrases.english: He said to me: One who has relations with minor girls will prove it,
phrases.notes: He means minor girls who are in a נדה state.

phrases.english: for there is only one prohibition there,
phrases.notes: Only the man is prohibited, because a minor is not obligated in מצוות.

phrases.english: and he is liable for each and every one!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לִי: הַבָּא עַל הַקְּטַנּוֹת יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's objection in step 15 by bringing a counterexample.
steps.raayaObject: That the 'two prohibitions' of נדה is not what makes each act liable separately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of relations with a minor נדה: one prohibition, yet liable for each act.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: minors will be prohibited later, שבת never
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the minor case: she will be prohibited when she grows up, but שבת will never have a second prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: You can say that about minor girls, who, even though they are not prohibited now, will be prohibited later. But can you say it about שבת, which has a second prohibition neither now nor later?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back on the minor-girl proof. He shows that the minor case is still different from שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the minor has no prohibition now, she will have one when she grows up. So the minor case still has some connection to 'two prohibitions.' שבת never has a second prohibition at any time, so the proof from minors does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, at present
Later on, here meaning once she grows up

phrases.english: I said to him: If you said this about minor girls,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן עַכְשָׁיו –
phrases.english: where even though they do not have it now –
phrases.notes: "It" is the second prohibition, the one on the woman herself.

phrases.english: they will have it later,
will you say it about Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ עַכְשָׁיו וְלֹא לְאַחַר זְמַן?
phrases.english: which does not have it now nor later?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתִּי לוֹ: אִם אָמַרְתָּ בַּקְּטַנּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי אליעזר's proof from minor girls in step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A minor will have a second prohibition when she grows up; שבת never has one.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings a proof from relations with an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר argues that relations with an animal proves his point: there is never a second prohibition there, yet a person is liable for each act.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: One who has relations with an animal will prove it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא is still telling the story. Now רבי אליעזר brings a new case to show that you can be liable for each act even when there is only one prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא had rejected the minor נדה case because she will become forbidden in another way when she grows up. An animal will never have a second prohibition, just like שבת. If a person is still liable for each act with an animal, then the same should be true for each act on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: one who has relations with an animal
will prove (it); a case brought as a counter-example

phrases.english: He said to me:
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא is still speaking. 'He' is רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: One who has relations with an animal will prove it!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל הַבְּהֵמָה יוֹכִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A replacement proof after the minor נדה case was rejected in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That a person can be liable for each act even when only one prohibition is involved, so each act on שבת should also need its own חטאת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of relations with an animal, which never has a second prohibition.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא answers that the animal case is just like שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the proof: to him, the animal case is just as uncertain as שבת, so it cannot prove anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: I said to him: The animal is like שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back. He says the animal case is not a settled rule he accepts; he has the same doubt about it as about שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only prove an unclear case from a case that both sides agree on. רבי עקיבא does not accept as settled that a person is liable for each act with an animal; for him it is an open question. So the animal case has the same question mark as שבת and cannot serve as proof. This ends the debate in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: the animal is like שבת: it is just as unclear, so it cannot prove anything

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is not saying the animal case is lenient. He means it is just as much in doubt as שבת, so you cannot learn one from the other.

phrases.english: I said to him:
The animal is like שבת.
phrases.notes: He means: I have the same question about the animal case as about שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבְּהֵמָה כַּשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the animal proof from step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the animal case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The animal case is itself in doubt, just like שבת, so it cannot settle the question.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what exactly רבי עקיבא was asking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what precise question רבי עקיבא put to רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What was he asking him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה. It is setting up its next move by asking what exactly רבי עקיבא's question was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's case has two parts: many תולדות of one מלאכה, and many שבתות. It is not clear which part was the real point of his question. The next steps will test each option.

keyTerms.meaning: the Talmud's discussion of the משנה
what was he asking him? what was the exact question?

phrases.english: GEMARA: What was he asking him?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי עקיבא and 'him' is רבי אליעזר, from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָבָעֵי מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis of the question in the משנה (step 13).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which issue was רבי עקיבא really asking about: the many שבתות, or the many תולדות?

steps.title: If he asked only about many שבתות, he should have used a simpler case
steps.stepSummary: Suggestion: he asked whether separate שבתות count like separate people. Challenge: then he should have asked about one מלאכה done on many שבתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was asking him whether שבתות are like separate bodies or not, let him ask: one who does a single מלאכה on many שבתות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first option: maybe רבי עקיבא only wanted to know whether each שבת counts on its own. It rejects this, because then there was no reason to add the many תולדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With נדה, relations with separate women count as separate sins. The question would be whether separate שבתות are like separate women. To ask that cleanly, one מלאכה on many שבתות is enough. Adding many kinds of תולדות only clutters the question.

keyTerms.meaning: are separate שבתות like separate bodies (people), so each counts on its own?
let him ask (it this way)
one מלאכה done on many שבתות

phrases.english: If whether שבתות are like separate bodies
phrases.notes: Like being with several different נדה women, where each one counts separately.

phrases.english: or not, is what he was asking him,
let him ask:
one who does a single מלאכה on many שבתות!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי שַׁבָּתוֹת כְּגוּפִין דָּמְיָין וְאִי לָא בָּעֵי מִינֵּיהּ, נִיבְעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible meaning of the question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי עקיבא's question was only about many שבתות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the extra detail of many תולדות is unnecessary; a simpler case would ask the question cleanly.

steps.title: If he asked only about תולדות, he should have used one שבת
steps.stepSummary: Second suggestion: he asked whether תולדות count like separate אבות. Challenge: then he should have asked about many תולדות on a single שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he was asking him whether תולדות of מלאכות are like אבות or not. Then let him ask: one who does many מלאכות of the same type as one מלאכה on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the second option: maybe the question was only about תולדות. It rejects this too, because then there was no reason to mention many שבתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing two different אבות מלאכות makes you liable twice. The question would be whether two תולדות of the same אב count like two separate אבות. That is asked best with one שבת, so mentioning many שבתות only clutters the case.

keyTerms.meaning: תולדות: sub-types that come from a main מלאכה
the main categories of מלאכה
of the same type as one main מלאכה

phrases.english: Rather:
whether the sub-types of מלאכות are like the main categories
or not, is what he was asking him,
let him ask him:
one who does many מלאכות
of the same type as one מלאכה, on שבת!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת אִי כְּאָבוֹת דָּמְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first option fails, offers and rejects the second option.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי עקיבא's question was only about תולדות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If so, the many שבתות are unnecessary; one שבת would ask the question cleanly.

steps.title: רבא: רבי עקיבא asked two questions at once
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes בי רב: רבי עקיבא asked both questions together, about many שבתות and about תולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They say in the school of רב: He asked him two things. He asked whether שבתות are like separate bodies or not, and whether תולדות of מלאכות are like the main מלאכות or not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the puzzle. רבי עקיבא's case mentions both details because he was asking both questions at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the last two steps assumed only one question and found an extra detail. Once we say there were two questions, both details are needed: many שבתות for the first question, and many תולדות for the second.

keyTerms.meaning: the school (study house) of רב
two (things/questions)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's one case holds two questions: (1) do separate שבתות count like separate people? (2) do תולדות of one אב count like separate אבות? That is why his case has both many שבתות and many תולדות.

phrases.english: רבא said: They say in the school of Rav,
he asked him two things:
whether שבתות are like separate bodies
or not, he asked him,

phrases.aramaic: וַלְדֵי מְלָאכוֹת כִּמְלָאכוֹת דָּמְיָין אִי לָא.
phrases.english: and whether sub-types of מלאכות are like the main מלאכות or not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב, תַּרְתֵּי בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 and solves both difficulties in steps 21 and 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation: the question is understood as two questions joined together.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא asked only one question, so one detail in his case seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: He asked two questions together, so both many שבתות and many תולדות are needed in the case.

steps.title: Which case of many שבתות was the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which kind of mistake the many-שבתות question was about. First possibility: he forgot it was שבת, so the days in between obviously separate the sins. Then the real question is the case where he knew it was שבת, and whether each שבת counts as a separate 'body'.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the שבתות, what exactly was he asking? Maybe in a case of forgetting it was שבת but knowing the work is forbidden, it was obvious to him that the weekdays in between count as awareness and split the sins. So his question was about knowing it was שבת but not knowing the work is forbidden: are separate שבתות like separate bodies or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of mistake רבי עקיבא's question about many שבתות was talking about. It starts by suggesting the first of two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can make two kinds of mistake. He can forget that today is שבת, or he can know it is שבת but not know that this work is forbidden. In the first suggestion, if he forgot it was שבת, the weekdays in between clearly split his sins. So the open question would only be the other case: does each שבת count as its own separate 'body', the way separate people do?

keyTerms.meaning: How exactly was he asking? What was the precise case?
He forgot it was שבת, but he knew the work is forbidden
He knew it was שבת, but he did not know the work is forbidden
The weekdays in between the שבתות
Awareness that splits sins into separate groups, each needing its own חטאת
Are they like separate bodies, each counted on its own?

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two mistakes apart. 'שגגת שבת' means he forgot what DAY it is. 'שגגת מלאכות' means he did not know the LAW about the work. The whole question depends on which one he got wrong.

phrases.english: And about the שבתות, how exactly was he asking?
In a case where he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden,
it was obvious to him that the days in between
count as awareness that splits the sins,
and in a case where he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden
that is what he asked him about:
are they like separate bodies or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׁבָּתוֹת, הֵיכִי מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא said in step 23 that רבי עקיבא asked about many שבתות. Now the גמרא asks exactly which case of many שבתות he meant.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of mistake (forgetting the day, or not knowing the law) was רבי עקיבא's question about?

steps.title: The opposite possibility: the question was about the days in between
steps.stepSummary: Or maybe the opposite is true. When he knew it was שבת, it was obvious that separate שבתות count as separate bodies. The real question was the case where he forgot it was שבת: do the weekdays in between split the sins or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps when he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden, it was obvious to him that the שבתות are like separate bodies. His question was about forgetting it was שבת while knowing the work was forbidden: do the days in between count as awareness that splits the sins, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second side of its question by flipping the first suggestion around. Now it is left with two options and needs someone to decide between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here, the 'separate bodies' idea is treated as already clear. The doubt moves to the forgetting-שבת case: do the weekdays between the שבתות count as awareness that splits the sins? The two suggestions mirror each other, so the גמרא needs an answer about which case was clear and which was the doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
Obvious. This part needs no question.

phrases.english: Or perhaps,
in a case where he knew it was שבת but did not know the work was forbidden,
it was obvious to him that they are like separate bodies,
and in a case where he forgot it was שבת but knew the work was forbidden
that is what he asked him about:
whether the days in between count
as awareness that splits the sins, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא, זְדוֹן שַׁבָּת וְשִׁגְגַת מְלָאכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the opposite side of the question in step 24. It swaps which case was obvious and which case was the real doubt.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Was רבי עקיבא unsure about the 'separate bodies' idea, or about whether the days in between split the sins?

steps.title: רבה begins his answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה starts to answer which case רבי עקיבא was asking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up the next move: רבה is about to answer the question from steps 24 and 25. His actual words come right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא has two possible readings of רבי עקיבא's question. רבה's answer, which comes next, will tell us which case was obvious to רבי עקיבא and which case he was unsure about.

phrases.english: רבה said:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This opens the answer to the two-sided question in steps 24 and 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not yet given. רבה's actual answer comes right after this line.
